title: Tree That Mirrors Itself
statement:
You get the root of a binary tree. Return true if the tree is its own mirror image: if you folded it along a vertical line through the root, every node on the left would land on a node with the same value on the right, and the shapes would match exactly.

Trees are written in level order with null for a missing child.

examples.why: The outer pair (7 and 7) and the inner pair (1 and 1) both match.
Both subtrees have the same values in the same order, but that is a copy, not a mirror. The left's outer 7 faces the right's outer 1.
The values look balanced, but the 5s are both right children. In a mirror one must be a left child.

constraints: The tree is at most 500 levels deep
hints: Comparing the left subtree to the right subtree directly checks for a copy, not a mirror. What should the left subtree's left child be compared with?
Two trees A and B are mirrors when their roots match, A.left mirrors B.right, and A.right mirrors B.left.
Write a helper on two nodes that returns true when both are null, false when exactly one is null or the values differ, and otherwise recurses on the outer pair and the inner pair.

explain.intuition:
Folding the tree along its middle puts the left subtree on top of the right subtree, flipped. So the real question is about two trees: is the left subtree the mirror of the right one?

Two trees are mirrors when their roots have the same value, the outer children match (left of the first with right of the second), and the inner children match (right of the first with left of the second). That gives a recursive helper on a pair of nodes. The same pairs can also be checked with a queue: push pairs, pop one, compare it, push its outer and inner pairs.
steps: In mirror(a, b): if both are null, return true. If only one is null, return false.
pitfalls: Checking that the left and right subtrees are equal. The second example has equal subtrees and is not symmetric.
Comparing level-order lists of values and ignoring the nulls. The third example has matching values on every level but the wrong shape.
Comparing only values and not the presence of children: one side having a child where the other has null already breaks the symmetry.

complexity.space: O(h) recursive, O(width) with a queue

solutions.title: Recursive pair check
solutions.idea: A helper compares two nodes and recurses on the outer pair and the inner pair.

solutions.title: Queue of pairs
solutions.idea: Push pairs of nodes that must match. Pop a pair, compare it, push its outer and inner pairs.

followups: Check whether two separate trees are mirrors of each other. How much of this code changes?
Count how many subtrees of the tree are symmetric. Can you do it in one pass?
